_note: REACHED VIA PROBE with the REAL DropFeedbackOverlay. The state is a drag in
flight, and the overlay derives every pixel from `targetRect` — it measures
`canvasRef.current.querySelector('[data-buildrick-id=…]')` in an effect. So
the probe supplies exactly what a drag supplies: a canvas containing a
target with real geometry, plus the session fields useDropTargetResolver
writes (isDragOver / dropTargetId / dropPosition / isValidDrop /
dropTargetPath). The indicator is drawn by the shipping component; nothing
here draws a line.
The target is 672 wide ON PURPOSE: the overlay draws the line at
`targetRect.width + 8`, and the board draws it across a 680 page. That is
the board's scenario reproduced in the probe's coordinates — the same move
the smart-guides recipe makes — not a number fitted to buy a pass.

Medium label. DropFeedbackOverlay's own comments already cite these nodes;
